architecture: error.rs is built incrementally, variant-group by variant-group, in AC-001's exact declared order. Every task T-001..T-008 performs a FULL overwrite of error.rs (not an append) with the complete cumulative content through that task, so the enum's closing brace is present at the end of every commit -- the file is always syntactically well-formed (balanced braces) even though the crate as a whole cannot yet build (see baseline_build_status). Each task's 'confirm green' step diffs the ENTIRE file against the complete expected content -- never a sed-extracted line range -- so there is no brittle line-number target that can silently drift out of sync; if content differs, the diff output shows exactly where. Verification for the 12 criteria whose doc comments describe facts about the design corpus (construction-site counts, exact literals elsewhere in docs/spec/*.md, call-chain structure) is split into two layers: a content-exactness diff/grep against error.rs itself (proving the file was written as intended), and a SEPARATE grounding check against the independent, pre-existing docs/spec/*.md files (proving the doc comment's claims are actually true of the design corpus, not merely self-consistent with prose the same step just typed). T-009 is a documentation-only task -- it writes zero Rust, claims zero acceptance criteria, and exists solely to record why the Io variant (AC-001's 14th variant) and AC-004 in full cannot be implemented in this track; both are tracked in this plan's top-level deferred_criteria field so neither is ever silently treated as satisfied. T-010 adds real `assert_eq!` Display-text tests for the 13 non-Io variants directly in error.rs, and proves all 13 pass via an isolated /tmp fixture crate with no io-errors/registry dependency -- the same isolation pattern SPEC-004/PLAN-004 already established for this exact class of blocker (confirmed by inspecting PLAN-004.json's own T-020 through T-022, which use isolated /tmp fixtures with real cargo runs for behavioral criteria that the real manifest cannot exercise). The Io variant's own Display/source() test (AC-004) is explicitly deferred and documented as such, not silently omitted.

baseline_build_status.summary: Real `cargo build`/`check`/`test` against the actual crates/monokl manifest cannot succeed yet, for TWO independent, already-diagnosed, pre-existing reasons unrelated to this plan's own scope. Neither is introduced by this plan and neither is fixed by it. lambda-recon should NOT treat either failure as a signal to abort -- both are expected.
baseline_build_status.reason_1_registry: crates/monokl/Cargo.toml:43 declares `io-errors = { path = "../io-errors", version = "0.1", registry = "orin-cargo", default-features = false }`. No `crates/io-errors/` directory exists anywhere in this workspace, and no `.cargo/config.toml` `[registries.orin-cargo]` entry exists either. This is the same gap SPEC-004's AC-008B documented and PLAN-004 already worked around; empirically, `cargo metadata`/`build`/ `check` against any manifest containing `registry = "orin-cargo"` fails at manifest PARSE time (`registry index was not found in any configuration: `orin-cargo``), before dependency resolution or network access, independent of whether ../io-errors exists.
baseline_build_status.reason_2_missing_modules: This reason is NEW to this plan's own review pass and was independently confirmed by reading the real files on disk, not assumed from a prior gate's characterization: crates/monokl/src/lib.rs declares 15 total module statements (14 `pub mod` -- analysis, budget, cli, dedup, enrich, error, indices, output, pipeline, query, rank, text_search, tokens, types -- plus 1 non-pub `#[cfg(test)] mod tests_types`), and only lib.rs itself exists as a file in crates/monokl/src/ -- error.rs (this plan's own target) does not exist until T-001 creates it, and none of the other 13 pub modules or tests_types exists at all. Separately, crates/monokl/Cargo.toml:18-21 declares `[[bin]] name = "monokl" path = "src/main.rs" required-features = ["cli"]`, and src/main.rs does not exist either. This means the crate is unbuildable independent of the io-errors/registry gap entirely -- even with a working registry and a real io-errors crate, `cargo build` would still fail on `error[E0583]: file not found for module` for every undeclared sibling module, and `cargo build --bin monokl --features cli` would fail with a missing src/main.rs. Creating those sibling module files and main.rs is explicitly out of scope for this plan (SPEC-001 covers only error.rs's MonoklError enum and Result<T> alias); each sibling module's own track (persist.rs, git_scope.rs, io_safety.rs, cli.rs, etc.) owns creating its own file.
baseline_build_status.what_lambda_recon_should_check_instead: Do not run `cargo build`/`check`/`test` against the real crates/monokl manifest as a baseline gate for this plan -- it is expected to fail for the two reasons above, neither of which this plan's tasks introduce or are responsible for fixing. Instead: (1) every task in this plan from T-001 through T-008 (NOT T-010 -- see below) verifies error.rs's content via `diff`/`grep` against exact expected text, plus a brace-balance sanity check (`{` count == `}` count) confirming the file is always structurally well-formed Rust at every commit (matching the pattern SPEC-004/PLAN-004 already established for this exact class of blocker); (2) T-010 is explicitly EXCLUDED from the brace-balance heuristic: once T-010 appends its `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block, one test helper deliberately constructs an invalid-JSON string literal, `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>("{not valid json")`, whose lone `{` character is not a real brace and throws off a naive `grep -o '{' | wc -l` vs `grep -o '}' | wc -l` count (65 open vs 64 close on the real T-010 file content -- now including the 14th, `#[cfg(feature = "miette")]`-gated `all_non_io_variants_have_no_diagnostic_metadata` test, which this plan's fourth review round moved into the committed file itself rather than leaving it fixture-only; confirmed empirically) even though the file compiles and all its tests pass. T-010's OWN real `cargo test` run (its step 6, executed against the isolated /tmp fixture) is T-010's actual structural proof instead -- a stronger guarantee than a brace count, since it proves the file not just balanced but compiling and passing; (3) T-010 additionally proves the 13 non-Io variants' Display texts, plus AC-002B's non-Io behavioral half (code()/help()/url() == None), are correct, real, passing behavior by running actual `cargo test` (14 tests) inside an isolated /tmp fixture crate that has no io-errors/registry dependency at all, so it is unaffected by reason_1 and reason_2 above; (4) if lambda-recon wants a live syntax/type-check signal scoped to just this plan's own file, the isolated-fixture pattern in T-010 is the correct model to reuse -- not a scoped `cargo check --lib` against the real crate, which would still fail at manifest-parse time per reason_1 regardless of error.rs's own correctness.

AC-001 requires all 14 MonoklError variants; AC-004 requires the Io
variant's transparent Display/source() pass-through. Neither can be
implemented today: the io-errors crate this variant depends on does
not exist at ../io-errors despite being declared as a mandatory,
non-optional dependency in crates/monokl/Cargo.toml, and that same
dependency's registry = "orin-cargo" has no matching
.cargo/config.toml entry anywhere in this workspace. This is a
documentation-only commit -- it writes zero Rust and claims zero
acceptance criteria in covers_criteria; AC-001's Io-variant clause
and AC-004 in full are tracked in this plan's top-level
deferred_criteria field instead, so neither is ever silently treated
as satisfied. depends_on T-008 (not T-001) because the state this
file asserts -- 13/14 variants present, Result<T> alias in place --
only becomes true once T-008 completes.

tasks.title: error.rs: add real #[cfg(test)] Display-literal assertions for all 13 non-Io variants, proven via isolated cargo test fixture
steps: Write the failing test. This criterion set (every Display literal SPEC-001 locks, for the 13 non-Io variants) currently has zero runnable Rust assertions anywhere -- only grep-on-source checks. Confirm that gap exists first: `grep -c 'assert_eq!' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/error.rs || true` (before this task's write) expect `0`.
Confirm red: run the command above now. It prints `0`.

Now prove these 13 Display-literal tests, PLUS a 14th test proving AC-002B's behavioral half for the 13 non-Io variants (<MonoklError as miette::Diagnostic>::code()/help()/url() all return None), actually pass as real Rust, using an isolated /tmp fixture crate that reproduces the same enum and test module without the io-errors/registry dependency this plan's baseline_build_status note documents as blocking any real cargo invocation against the actual crates/monokl manifest -- the same isolation pattern SPEC-004/PLAN-004 already established for this exact class of blocker. The fixture adds `miette` as a plain dependency (not gated behind any feature of its own -- the fixture has no "miette" feature flag to gate on) and keeps `#[derive(miette::Diagnostic)]` unconditional on the fixture's copy of the enum, so the 14th test below can call `.code()`/`.help()`/`.url()` directly. Run: `rm -rf /tmp/plan001_ac_display_fixture && mkdir -p /tmp/plan001_ac_display_fixture/src && cat > /tmp/plan001_ac_display_fixture/Cargo.toml <<'TOMLEOF'
[package]
name = "ac_display_fixture"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[workspace]

[lib]
name = "ac_display_fixture"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[dependencies]
thiserror = "2"
camino = "1"
ignore = "0.4"
grep-regex = "0.1"
serde_json = "1"
miette = { version = "7", features = ["fancy"] }
TOMLEOF`

Confirm green for real. Run: `out=$( (cd /tmp/plan001_ac_display_fixture && cargo test) 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out" | tail -20; echo "exit=$rc"`. Expected output (captured live against cargo 1.96.0 during this plan's own construction, not guessed -- 14 tests now, not 13, because of the added AC-002B diagnostic-metadata test): the test summary line `test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in ...s` and `exit=0`. Assert precisely: `echo "$out" | grep -q '14 passed; 0 failed' && echo FOURTEEN_PASSED` expect `FOURTEEN_PASSED`; `[ "$rc" = 0 ] && echo EXIT_OK` expect `EXIT_OK`. Clean up: `rm -rf /tmp/plan001_ac_display_fixture`.

The Io variant's own Display/source()-pass-through test (AC-004) is explicitly NOT included above and is not run anywhere by this task -- it cannot be, since the Io variant does not exist in this enum yet (blocked, see T-009) and FileIoError (the type it would need to construct a real test instance) does not exist on disk either. This is a deferred, currently-unrunnable test, not an oversight: once T-009's blocker is resolved and the Io variant is added, its test belongs in the same #[cfg(test)] mod tests block this task just wrote, following the same real-assertion pattern (construct a real FileIoError, wrap it in MonoklError::Io, assert_eq! the Display text against one of the four literals AC-004 names, and assert std::error::Error::source() returns Some matching the wrapped io::Error). Likewise, AC-002B's Io-variant clause (<MonoklError as miette::Diagnostic>::code()/help()/url() == None specifically for the Io variant) is out of scope for the 14th test this task adds above -- that test covers only the 13 non-Io variants. Once the Io variant exists, its Diagnostic assertions belong alongside its Display/source() test in the same block, using the same real-fixture pattern this task establishes.
Commit.
tasks.commit_message:
test(monokl): add real assert_eq! Display-literal tests for MonoklError's 13 non-Io variants, plus an AC-002B Diagnostic test

Replaces grep-only verification of each variant's #[error(...)] text
with real, runnable Rust assertions, and adds a 14th test proving
AC-002B's behavioral half for these 13 variants: <MonoklError as
miette::Diagnostic>::code()/help()/url() all return None. These
cannot execute inside the real monokl crate yet (see
baseline_build_status: the crate cannot build independent of
io-errors, for unrelated pre-existing reasons), so this commit also
proves all 14 pass for real via an isolated /tmp fixture crate with
no io-errors/registry dependency -- the same isolation pattern
SPEC-004/PLAN-004 established for this class of blocker. The
fixture adds miette as a plain dependency and keeps
#[derive(miette::Diagnostic)] unconditional on its copy of the enum
(no "miette" feature of its own to gate on). The Io variant's own
Display and Diagnostic tests are explicitly deferred (T-009): it
cannot be constructed without FileIoError, which does not exist.
